items.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
items.summary: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inhe…

items.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in …

items.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
items.summary: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, wh…

items.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose…

items.title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
items.summary: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the student weigh candidate emotions against it. In Meta-Harness Evolving (MHE), a stronger LLM, the Builder, reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits the harness; static checks an…

items.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
items.summary: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks across different levels. We evaluate six models across 150 runs with 24-hour budgets, totaling over 10,000 GPU-hours. Our results show that model rankings vary with the evaluation horizon, while 135 of the 150 runs achieve further improvements during the second half of their budgets. These findings indicate that shorter evaluations can overlook both optimization gains and changes …

items.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
items.summary: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. In this paper, we introduce an exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means with mini-batch updates, powered by modern deep learning machinery and new insights. We also establish scaling laws on how decay rate and batch size impact final performance. This gives us a formulaic rule to fix them for multiple problem sizes and embedding datasets, without the need for any hyperparameter sweep. The resulting clustering algorithm, coined …

items.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
items.summary: Large language models can generate motion graphics from static images and natural language requests, but it remains difficult to evaluate how well models can follow requests that combine spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements. We introduce MotionGraphicsBench, an expert-curated benchmark of 100 instances for animating an input static SVG with a motion edit prompt. By supplying all required visual elements, our editing task reflects a designer-like workflow and isolates motion generation from graphic generation. Derived from real-world Lottie motion designs, our benchmark contains diver…

items.title: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
items.summary: We introduce FraudBench, an evaluation of large language models' (LLMs) propensities to recommend, assist, or directly take actions that would constitute fraud under U.S. law. Our evaluation contains a novel dataset of 159 scenarios based on real-world U.S. court cases and validated by legal experts. We present each scenario to LLMs via three tasks at varying levels of autonomy: advising users, drafting messages for users to send, and acting directly on behalf of users (477 tasks total). In each scenario, FraudBench re-enacts the facts of a court case to give LLMs an opportunity, but no explic…

items.title: onóna: Twin Embeddings with Tied Unembeddings
items.summary: Weight tying reduces the parameter cost of language models, but the usual tied output head is limited to a single softmax. We introduce onóna, a two-table parameterization that increases output expressiveness while preserving input-output weight sharing. The Transformer takes the average of two embedding tables as input, and the output head combines the softmax distributions defined by those same tables. A gate conditioned only on the current input token determines the mixture weight. Its values can be precomputed for inference, and the Transformer body remains unchanged. We evaluate onóna acr…

items.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
items.summary: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction. The design follows YOCO and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, where the projection is trained into the model. RidgeFill retrofits it onto models that were never trained for it: the map is a ridge regression fitted once in closed form from one pass over calibration text, the layer's own projections run unchanged, and a chosen set of rows…

items.title: Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox
items.summary: Many of the most consequential advances promised by AI, from curing diseases and inventing new technologies to formulating new scientific theories, are fundamentally creative acts. Yet creativity is uniquely difficult to learn because it faces a creative paradox: learning to repeat past examples of creative success makes those specific examples more likely to recur, inhibiting the very creativity desired. This work argues that creativity is better modeled as an explicit process rather than as a property of individual artifacts, and proposes to learn the underlying generative principles behind …

items.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
items.summary: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to…

items.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
items.summary: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. LCM-Promo is a task-specific Large Commerce Model (LCM): a finetuned LLM trained on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and promotion response. It learns monotonic promotion-response curves from production logs by interpreting single-token outputs as conversion-threshold probabilities, while conditioning on session context such as day and delivery shift. In a production A/B test on churn reactivation, LCM-Promo increased conversion by 1% and reduced promotion cost by 6% relative to the Segment-EMA producti…

items.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
items.summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demon…

items.title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language models can interpret instructions and plan manipulation tasks, yet struggle when acting directly as robot policies. On RoboDojo, a large planning-execution gap separates high-level task decisions from physical execution: removing arm execution raises GPT-6 Astra's success rate from 22.5% under the reference control interface to 76.2%. We present Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness that closes 68.3% of this gap in zero-shot manipulation without target-task trials or resets. In Auriga, the model makes all task decisions over an explicit task belief and acts through either direc…

items.title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
items.summary: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniq…

items.title: Energy-Tweedie: Score meets Score, Energy meets Energy
items.summary: Denoising and score estimation are classically linked through Tweedie's formula, which relates the posterior mean under Gaussian noise to the Stein score of the noisy marginal. In this work, we extend this perspective beyond Gaussian noise to a broad class of Gibbs (energy-based) noise distributions, with the generalized Gaussian family as an example. We derive the Energy-Tweedie identity: when the denoising posterior is viewed through the lens of scoring rules, the path derivative of a kernel scoring rule defined by the noise potential recovers the Stein score of the noisy marginal. Thus, the…

items.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
items.summary: Challenging repository-level benchmarks remain limited for many programming language ecosystems, where filtering scarce candidates with ambiguous descriptions or defective tests can discard valuable engineering problems. We introduce Longtail-SWE, a benchmark of 202 issue-resolution tasks across 13 languages with limited coverage in existing repository-level benchmarks: Clojure, Dart, Elixir, Erlang, F#, Haskell, Julia, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, R, Scala, and Swift. Its construction uses a solver--judge--repairer pipeline: a solver attempts each candidate task, and a judge reviews the task together …

items.title: SkinMind: Equipping Agentic RAG with Human-Inspired Graph Probing for Reliable Dermatology AI
items.summary: Reliable dermatology AI requires access to verifiable evidence distributed across heterogeneous textual and visual sources. However, conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically relies on one-shot retrieval from flat corpora, limiting its ability to adapt retrieval granularity, explore multi-hop relations, and integrate multimodal clinical evidence. We introduce SkinMind, a multimodal agentic RAG framework that equips policy models with human-inspired graph probing for autonomous evidence seeking. SkinMind organizes retrieval as an iterative interaction between an orchestrator a…

items.title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
items.summary: Self-supervised learning in Vision Transformer models, such as DINO, enables robust visual perception without requiring labeled data by leveraging large-scale image datasets. However, these models lack a focusing mechanism during training, resulting in perceptual representations that are often ambiguous or overly similar. In this work, we introduce two visual focusing loss functions designed to establish correspondence between the model's attention and specific regions within images. Specifically, we leverage the multi-head attention mechanism within the model to selectively steer the model's …

items.title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
items.summary: While Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) accelerates isolated algorithm and kernel synthesis, distributed LLM training depends on tightly coupled launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules, where single edits often hit out-of-memory (OOM) boundaries, compiler conflicts, measurement jitter, or silent numerical drift. We present InfraRSI, the agentic harness that turns open-ended human commands into verified training optimizations via a five-stage workflow: init locks editable scope and a fixed task contract over workload, loss, and timing invariants to prevent reward hacking, …

items.title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
items.summary: Real-time 3D human mesh recovery from a single image on mobile devices is a challenging problem with many applications, including robotics, biomechanics, AR/VR, and exergames. Current state-of-the-art models are either too slow to run efficiently on mobile devices or sacrifice accuracy for speed. We present InstantHMR, a family of open-source single-image regressors suited for mobile inference, based on the Momentum Human Rig (MHR) parametric model and trained exclusively on publicly available annotations from the SAM 3D Body dataset. Our approach achieves remarkable performance on a Samsung G…

items.title: Spatial Harness: Grounding Spatial Reasoning in Executable World States with Physics Engines
items.summary: Spatial reasoning requires understanding how objects and observers are arranged in a scene and how their relations change with viewpoint or movement. Vision-language models (VLMs) typically perform both steps through model-internal reasoning, forming an implicit scene interpretation from partial views and imagining the consequences of spatial transformations. A misread scene can lead to a wrong answer, while even a correct interpretation does not ensure that imagined transformations satisfy spatial constraints. We introduce Spatial Harness, which represents scenes as explicit and executable wo…

items.title: Seeing the Small: Deformable Duality Mamba for Retinal Lesion Segmentation
items.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) lesions vary widely in shape, and microaneurysms (MAs) span only a few pixels. We hypothesize that modeling the spatial organization of lesion regions, with global context and shape-adaptive scanning, improves the segmentation of such small and irregular lesions. To test this, we propose D$^2$Mamba, which couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning. We evaluate it with five-fold cross-validation on the DDR dataset, comparing against representative segmentation baselines under an identical training protocol, and conduct ablations on each compo…

items.title: Evidential Deep Learning with conditional entropy for glaucoma detection
items.summary: We propose a novel conditional entropy function as a basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. Using the EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL datasets for validation, we found that our proposed EDL model regularized by conditional entropy function produced uncertainty estimates with substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and the conventional EDL framework based on Dempster uncertainty. To further probe our models' interpretability, we analyzed Grad-CAM…

items.title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
items.summary: Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. We study how to adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC model, using a 172.8-hour corpus covering six Nepali speech domains. Its pretrained tokenizer does not support digits and several common symbols. Rather than replace it or discard these recordings, we generate Nepali and English readings for numbers and use zero-shot ASR output to select a plausible form. Full fine-tuning reduces test word error rate…

items.title: TMAL: Topology-preserving Multi-offset Affinity Learning for Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
items.summary: Curvilinear structures such as retinal vessels and surface cracks need both pixel-level accuracy and structural continuity. Pixel-wise supervision does not model the connections between pixels, and topology-based losses still produce ordinary masks. Connectivity-based methods predict these connections directly, but they use binary connectivity targets over a fixed local range. Such labels give the same value to thin segments and to thick regions, and they cannot describe connections at larger offsets. items.title: Distribution Shift Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery using Machine Learning Models
items.summary: Remote sensing imagery acquired by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) supports wide range of applications; however, deploying machine learning (ML) models on resource-constrained aerial platforms introduces challenges beyond predictive accuracy, particularly when deployment data differ from the distributions observed during training. Such shifts are common in remote sensing due to geographic, sensor, seasonal, and other visual variations. A practical solution is to equip deployed models with mechanisms that detect emerging distribution shifts and support subsequent responsive actions. This paper …

items.title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
items.summary: Small language models (SLMs) running on mobile devices can keep user data private and work without connectivity. But they perform well only when fine-tuned for the target task and sized for the target device, a process that today requires repeated expert tuning. We present {\it Mobile AI Factory}, an agentic system that builds a fine-tuned, quantized SLM for a given task and phone. Given a task specification and a target phone, an orchestrator LLM chooses whether to tune hyperparameters, mine real data, or generate synthetic examples, while fixed rules roll back changes that hurt accuracy. The…

items.title: Dark Matters: VAE-Aware HDR Encoding for SDR-to-HDR Video Reconstruction
items.summary: SDR-to-HDR reconstruction is an ill-posed problem in which clipped highlights, crushed shadows, and quantization artifacts must be recovered while preserving the original content. Latent diffusion models provide powerful generative priors for restoring missing detail, but their effectiveness is constrained by how HDR signals pass through the pretrained VAE. We find that common log-like encodings suppress low-luminance chromatic differences before generation, producing a dark-side collapse in the frozen-VAE latent. We introduce EquivFlow, a compact, invertible exposure-equivariant encoding that…

items.title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
items.summary: Compositional generalization is an important form of out-of-distribution generalization, defined as the ability to train on some combinations of modules (e.g., functions such as sort, filter) and then generalize to unseen combinations. Despite substantial empirical work evaluating compositional generalization in transformers, findings have been inconsistent because evaluations were often conducted on a limited set of train-test splits, defined in an ad hoc manner. items.title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
items.summary: Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation (OV-SGG) requires models to recognize visual relationships beyond the training vocabulary, yet existing methods often rely on dataset-specific object--predicate co-occurrence patterns. Under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization, such reliance leads to biased, entangled relation representations, limiting both rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates. To address these challenges, we propose RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework that transforms MLLM-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) ra…

items.title: Simultaneous Near-Optimal Region Identification in Continuous Simulation Optimization: Minimax Complexity and Adaptive Sampling
items.summary: Simulation optimization typically returns a single estimated optimal point. When decisions also depend on criteria evaluated independently of simulation, such as resource cost, the decision maker instead needs the set of designs whose expected performance lies within a tolerance of the optimum, often choosing the tolerance only after seeing the tradeoffs. We study how to identify these near-optimal regions on a continuous design space, simultaneously for all tolerances up to a prescribed maximum $T$, with region estimation error at most $η$. items.title: When Reconstruction Helps Event-Camera Person Triggers
items.summary: Event cameras record asynchronous changes in brightness. To use a general visual model as a recording trigger, a system must represent these measurements in a form the model can interpret. We compare direct grayscale accumulation, two temporal encodings, and two intensity reconstructors on paired real event data. On 192 windows from four held-out DSEC recordings, thresholds calibrated only on development data yielded 40 of 52 person detections and 12 of 140 background positives with E2VID. items.summary: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. items.title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video
items.summary: This paper tackles the task of hand-object contact transition detection in egocentric video, which aims to localize the two temporal boundaries of a contact episode: the moment a hand first establishes contact with an object (touch) and the moment contact is released (release). We propose a unified framework that jointly models the interacting hand and object to accurately localize both transition types. The proposed framework augments hand-centric spatiotemporal representations with object-aware features learned directly from the video and introduces a transition-aware event spotting formulat…

items.title: Differentially Private Statistical Inference for Rankings from Pairwise Comparisons
items.summary: Reliable inference for rankings of large language models based on human pairwise comparisons must preserve the privacy of individual preference records. To meet this need, we develop methods for score and rank inference under the Bradley-Terry model with edge differential privacy. For an objective-perturbed estimator, a new leave-one-out analysis establishes finite-sample bounds on Euclidean and entrywise estimation errors. items.title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: KL-regularized reinforcement learning, the objective behind maximum-entropy RL and RL from human feedback, is variational inference in the graphical model of "control as inference": the regularized optimal policy is a posterior over trajectories, and the suboptimality of a policy is $β$ times a KL divergence between path measures. items.title: [补送码] 我制作了 Mac 的活动追踪器「日影」
items.summary: ## 补送码 上一月在 V 站发的送码帖很快就被领完了，所以这次提供更多激活码：前 100 位可以领取永久激活码，100 位以后的留言可以领取有效期一年的激活码，每个激活码可以激活 2 台 Mac。 有需要的请留下邮箱，我会稍后发送激活邮件。欢迎提意见或 bug！ ## 功能介绍 我是一个喜欢记录各种事情的人，但是现有的记录软件不能满足我记录电脑活动的需求（ActivityWatch、Qbserve 不好看，Timing 太贵而且复杂。还有很多软件在我看来是过度记录，既占储存又费电……）。所以出于自己的记录需求，我制作了 Mac 上的原生活动记录 app「日影」。 我把易用和美观排在首位，「日影」会自动记录用户的活动，所以不需要占用精力，容易持续下来。并且通过键鼠活动和前台播放来推断用户是否在真的使用 Mac，以提高记录的精确性，同时不需要请求额外的系统权限。 在统计页面里，可以看到自己某天某月在做什么，看到自己的使用趋势等等。我花了不少精力来把页面做好看。 ![]( https://i.imgur.com/8eJM5eY.png) ![]( https://i.imgur.com/odR2phi.png) ![]( https://i.imgur.com/1A0eVt2.png) ![]( https://i.imgur.com/cnQEw5Z.png) ![]( https:/…

items.title: 再聊 A/封号，所有的伪装都是徒劳
items.summary: 根据最近半个月被封的十几个号 以及各种身边同事和 V 友的封号情况来看 A\是一定有能力能做到，在你登录的一瞬间识别你是否为 CN 用户 再不济，你最多几轮对话或者在支付的瞬间，将你正确的分类 我的感觉是，在识别出来之后。 这些用户将会全部放在一个池子里面。 然后根据各种行为加分扣分。当达到阈值直接封 并且这些行为是随时、动态、人工的调整 我感觉，tibo 有 reset 按钮，A\有封号滑块 这样可以随时，调整他们的封号策略 可能昨天有 KPI 的考核紧一点，今天又因为什么原因松一点 但是总之，所有没有被封的，不是因为你各种所谓的防封、伪装策略生效了 只是你目前在 Claude 眼里面属于取保候审人员 随时可以把你关进去！ 并且，你不知道自己的哪一个行为可能会触犯他 每天都要战战兢兢的度过！

items.title: 观 V 友相亲贴有感，分享一下我遇到的相亲女
items.summary: 原： https://global.v2ex.com/t/1254348?p=2 # 大纲 1 、和中介等她等了 1 小时（中介是所谓的熟人的熟人） 2 、上来先点一大堆吃不完的菜，最后让中介打包走大多数 3 、饭还没吃完中介要我发 200 块红包，我不发，然后还在那一直 BB 4 、女方是 90 年的，中介说成 97 年的 5 、最后冷淡收场了，临走前还在那装，一边拿出微信余额一边说什么这年头谁还没个几十万，男人太小气没有女人看得上你之类的话。 # 正文 起因是我妈托熟人介绍，然后所谓的熟人又转手找了个熟人介绍，一共中转了三层找到最终介绍人，这里称中介。 一开始我并不知道有几层，开车载第一个介绍人到了目的地，等了中介半小时又找人找了一会，等女方等了快一小时。 等到快中午女的终于来了，我一看脸像好像有一点点不像 97 年的，但也没太在意，看了下时间要吃饭了于是提议先去吃饭，这时女方主动说附近有她熟悉的店，那我心想也行吧，免得难找地方。 吃饭时我让女方点菜，没想到点了一大桌，总共才 4 个人，期间问了几句才知道是 90 年不是 97 年，她有个弟弟和我差不多大。 饭后中介开始要我发红包，这里我已经确定对面很有问题了，我没发，中介一直在说，女方全程玩手机，磨了半小时后我看大家都坐不住了提议结束饭局，下楼时女方还在明示，说什么女人都喜欢大气的男人。 到了外面女的见我还是不给于是打算不演了…

items.summary: ## 介绍 SSHYard 是一款免费开源的 SSH / SFTP 客户端，支持 macOS 、Windows 和 Linux ，在终端里操作、管理远程文件等，再让 AI 助手直接在主机上帮你工作，一个窗口全部搞定。 本软件是纯 Go 编写的（基于 MyGO)，而且纯原生渲染，无任何 WebView 等，速度和占用都很不错，欢迎使用体验和反馈！ ## 开源地址 - 官方网站： https://sshyard.com - 开源地址： https://github.com/Licoy/sshyard ## 功能 - **终端** - 多标签、分屏与终端搜索，标签可拖动排序和重命名 - 真彩色、宽字符、输入法，以及 tmux 、vim 、htop 鼠标操作 - 十套内置配色方案并可导入 `.itermcolors`，支持关键字高亮、行号与时间戳，可调光标、行高和字宽 - 多种输出编码，可按主机设置；⌘ / Ctrl + 点击打开终端中的网址 - 除 SSH 外还支持 Telnet 、串口和本地终端（ Windows 可选 PowerShell 、CMD 、Git Bash 与 WSL ） - 同一主机的多个面板共享连接，断线自动重连 - **工作区** - 系统监控、进程占用、主机详情、Docker 、tmux 、快捷指令、历史指令、广播指令和会话日志都是可拖拽窗格，可停靠到任意窗格旁或…

items.title: 突然收到律师函！一脸懵
items.summary: 今天早上摸鱼摸着摸着就看到邮箱来了新邮件 打开一看是律师函？？？一脸懵 UDRP 域名争议，案号 HK‑2602201 ，域名 `aiping.icu` 我是该域名原始注册人，在 Cloudflare 注册。收到 ADNDRC 香港办事处发来的 UDRP 投诉通知。 现状：我搭建的是**大模型 API 公开测评榜单网站**，和投诉方 [aiping.cn]( https://aiping.cn) 都不是同一个东西，对方是售卖 token 的。 注册域名的时候出于对公开 WHOIS 隐私泄露的顾虑，填写了占位虚拟注册信息，结果拿这点说我虚假信息。 投诉方主张自己拥有 “AIPING” 未注册商标，要求把域名转移过去，说我不是第一时间注册人，我看了 WHOIS 第一注册人就是我在 cf 上购买的时间。 答辩截止时间 **2026‑11‑30**，程序要求提交英文 Form‑R 答辩书。 有点懵，想请教大佬们 帮忙支招= =
